artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $P$ be a locally finite graded poset with a unique minimal element $\hat 0$ and rank function $\rho: P \to \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$. Let $P_n = \{x \in P : \rho(x) = n\}$ and let $\mathbb{Z}P$ denote the free abelian group on $P$. Define the up and down operators $U,D: \mathbb{Z}P \to \mathbb{Z}P$ by
\[ U(x) = \sum_{y\,\gtrdot\, x} y, \qquad D(x) = \sum_{y\,\lessdot\, x} y, \]
where $\gtrdot$ and $\lessdot$ denote covering relations. Given a sequence $r=(r_0,r_1,r_2,\dots)$ of nonnegative integers, $P$ is called an $r$-differential poset (or sequentially differential poset with rank-vector $r$) if for every $n\ge 0$,
\[ DU - UD = r_n I \qquad \text{on } \mathbb{Z}P_n. \]

It is known that:
(i) for any sequence $r$ there is at most one distributive lattice that is an $r$-differential poset, and we denote it $L(r)$ when it exists;
(ii) if $r$ is an arithmetic progression $r_n = a + n\Delta$, then the class of distributive $r$-differential lattices is closed under Cartesian products, and conversely if the Cartesian product of two sequentially differential posets each having at least two ranks is sequentially differential, then both factors and the product have rank-vectors that are arithmetic progressions with a common difference $\Delta$;
(iii) one must have $\Delta \le 0$, with $\Delta=0$ corresponding to the ordinary differential posets, and $\Delta<0$ forcing the lattice to be finite.

Two infinite families of finite distributive sequentially differential lattices with arithmetic-progression rank-vectors are known: the Cartesian powers of the $2$-element chain and the Cartesian powers of the $3$-element chain.

Question: Do there exist any finite distributive sequentially differential lattices whose rank-vector is an arithmetic progression, other than the Cartesian powers of the $2$-element chain and the $3$-element chain? More generally, completely classify all finite distributive sequentially differential lattices with arithmetic-progression rank-vectors having common difference $\Delta < 0$.

No published classification or construction of additional examples beyond Cartesian powers of the 2- and 3-element chains was found.
